title: Ex 2.5 #7 · Truth table for (P ∧ ∼P) ⇒ Q
prompt: Build a truth table for $(P \wedge \sim P) \Rightarrow Q$ and enter the truth value of the whole statement in each row.
answer_format: Four T/F values, one per row, top to bottom, like T F T T. Rows (P, Q) go TT, TF, FT, FF, as in the book. Helper columns are optional steps, like ~P : F F T T.
hints: P ∧ ∼P is false in every row. What is the truth value of an implication whose hypothesis is false?
P ⇒ Q is false only when the hypothesis is true and the conclusion is false.
solution: The hypothesis $P \wedge \sim P$ is false in every row.
An implication with a false hypothesis is true, so the column is T T T T: the statement is always true.

reference.note: This exact exercise, restated in ProofLab's words. Uses the truth tables for ∧, ∨, ∼, ⇒ and ⇔ (Sections 2.2–2.5).
